{
  "finding": {
    "finding_id": "incident_1003-F-t3-logs-cascade-01",
    "task_id": "t3-logs-cascade",
    "run_id": "run-077d2281e6b24db8b2030c97e87f389e",
    "incident_id": "incident_1003",
    "role": "logs",
    "claim": "The ERROR/WARN log query across backend, payment, redis, and gateway for 2026-10-01T11:30:00Z-12:30:00Z returned only a single record: a backend ERROR 'Request processing exceeded deadline' observed at 12:00:14Z. No connection-refused, connection-pool-exhaustion, upstream/external-timeout, or cache-unavailability signatures from redis, payment, gateway, or postgres were returned. This single local deadline symptom does not by itself identify which service first emitted failures.",
    "evidence_ids": ["incident_1003-E-003"],
    "relation": "neutral",
    "confidence_qualifier": "weak",
    "followup_question": "Do broader log queries that include WARN severity and all services return downstream connection-refused or upstream-timeout signatures that this single ERROR-only record did not expose?"
  },
  "hypotheses": [
    {
      "hypothesis_id": "incident_1003-H-backend-deadline-01",
      "culprit_service": "backend",
      "failure_mode": "backend_resource_saturation",
      "support_ids": ["incident_1003-E-003"],
      "against_ids": [],
      "predicted_observations": [
        "backend CPU, memory, or per-request latency metrics elevated during 2026-10-01T11:30:00Z-12:30:00Z relative to baseline",
        "backend throughput saturation or queue growth coincident with the 12:00:14Z deadline error",
        "no connection-refused or timeout errors emitted by redis, payment, gateway, or postgres in the same window"
      ],
      "status": "OPEN",
      "open_questions": [
        "Backend resource metrics were never queried, so the isolated deadline error cannot be distinguished from upstream dependency delay or an external timeout.",
        "A single 'Request processing exceeded deadline' log is a symptom and provides no observed mechanism, so this hypothesis remains unconfirmed pending resource metrics."
      ]
    }
  ],
  "requested_checks": [
    {
      "task_id": "t3-metrics-backend-latency",
      "role": "metrics",
      "question": "During 2026-10-01T11:30:00Z-12:30:00Z, are backend resource and latency metrics (CPU, memory, request latency, queue depth) elevated relative to baseline, and do any postgres or redis dependency metrics (connection counts, cache availability, timeouts) degrade concurrently?",
      "allowed_tools": ["query_metrics"],
      "filters": {
        "start_ts": "2026-10-01T11:30:00Z",
        "end_ts": "2026-10-01T12:30:00Z",
        "service": "backend",
        "metrics": ["cpu_usage", "memory_usage", "request_latency", "queue_depth"]
      },
      "reason": "The logs task returned only one backend deadline error and no downstream failure signatures. Resource and latency metrics are the strongest remaining discriminator between local backend resource saturation and an upstream dependency (redis/payment/postgres) degradation.",
      "expected_discriminator": "Elevated backend CPU/memory/latency with flat downstream metrics supports backend_resource_saturation; concurrent postgres connection or lock metrics favor a database-culprit mechanism; degraded redis availability metrics favor redis_unavailable; no metric degradation anywhere leaves no causal mechanism support."
    },
    {
      "task_id": "t3-logs-all-services-warn",
      "role": "logs",
      "question": "During 2026-10-01T11:30:00Z-12:30:00Z, do WARN and ERROR logs from redis, payment, gateway, and postgres contain connection-refused, connection-pool exhaustion, upstream/external timeout, or cache-unavailability signatures, and which service emits the earliest such record?",
      "allowed_tools": ["query_logs"],
      "filters": {
        "start_ts": "2026-10-01T11:30:00Z",
        "end_ts": "2026-10-01T12:30:00Z",
        "severity": "WARN,ERROR"
      },
      "reason": "The prior log query was filtered to backend ERROR records and returned a single symptom. Broadening severity and service coverage is needed to determine whether downstream services emitted failures that precede or follow the backend deadline error, establishing causal chronology.",
      "expected_discriminator": "Redis connection-refused or cache-error logs favor redis_unavailable; payment upstream/HTTP timeout logs favor payment_external_timeout; postgres connection/timeout logs favor a database-culprit mechanism; backend-only errors with no downstream records leave the local-symptom interpretation intact."
    }
  ]
}
